newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault shares fall on results warning.
newsitem.headline: Renault shares fall on results warning.

text.p: Shares in Renault opened lower on Friday after the company issued a fresh warning about its results, saying it expected to show a 1996 operating loss considerably above market estimates.
The shares were down 2.38 percent at 126.90 francs at 0913 GMT after opening at 126.30.
The bourse's CAC-40 index was 0.3 percent higher at the same time.

"In view the prevailing economic context, and despite the increase in revenues of the automobile division, reflecting a more positive trend which has been confirmed by a widening of the Renault market share in France in the early part of 1997, the operating loss to be reported by Renault Group for 1996 will be considerably higher than that generally anticipated by the financial markets," Renault said in its 1996 sales statement.

Renault did not say what it considered to be the market consensus. But one industry analyst said the market had been expected an operating loss of roughly two billion francs for the car division, an operating loss of around 600 million francs for the trucks and an operating profit of around 1.3 billion at the finance unit, for a total operating loss of 1.3 billion francs.
Renault said its 1996 consolidated sales were 184.08 billion francs, compared with 184.07 billion for 1995.
It has previously said it expected to lose money on both its car and truck operations.
